Handle two malformed inputs found by fuzzing

websocket: A compressed message that isn't valid deflate data raised an
uncaught zlib.error, which was logged with a traceback. Now it closes the
connection with code 1007.

simple_httpclient: When the stream failed with an error (such as a chunk
size line too long to read), on_connection_close raised it from the
connection's read loop, where it was logged as an uncaught exception and
the request failed only when it timed out. Now the error fails the request
right away.

test: Add a regression corpus of past security fixes

security_corpus_test.py sends the trigger input of each past server-side
security fix to a real HTTPServer and checks only the response and the
logs, so the tests survive rewrites of the parsers they cover. The three
quadratic-parsing fixes are checked for linear scaling end to end. Each
case fails on the release before its fix.

Expand performance testing in CI

maint: Add pre-tag checks and release instructions

maint/scripts/pre_tag_checks.py checks that the version number and release
notes match the tag about to be pushed, then runs the full tests, lint,
docs and coverage, and compares benchmarks with the previous release. It
passes on the commits of past tags (v6.5.0, v6.5.10, v6.6.0b1, v6.6.0rc1)
and reports each mismatch when given the wrong tag.

maint/RELEASING.md replaces the Release-instructions wiki page: tags and
branches, the release steps (now including the pre-tag checks),
pre-releases before every minor release, the deprecation rule (also in
CONTRIBUTING.md), and how security releases are prepared and checked
before the fix is public.

ci: Compare benchmarks with the base branch on every PR

maint/benchmark/ci_benchmark.py measures CPU time per unit for the parsers
(typical and worst-case headers, cookies, header params, multipart), the
websocket mask, xhtml_escape, and the server scenarios from
dos_benchmark.py (refactored so they can be called from other scripts).

compare_benchmarks.py runs it against two source trees. Each round starts
a worker process per tree and alternates measurements between them, so
both see the same machine conditions, and keeps the fastest result for
each. Anything more than 20% slower is measured again with twice as many
processes and fails only if that agrees, since one side occasionally gets
an unusually fast or slow process.

The new CI job runs the comparison against the PR's base branch, alongside
the full tests (it takes a little over a minute), and puts the table on
the run's summary page. It also fails if an adversarial input exceeds an
absolute budget in microseconds per byte. In repeated comparisons of a
tree with itself nothing failed (one benchmark needed a recheck); a 40%
slowdown in header parsing failed on the header benchmarks only.

test: Add memory budgets for more parsers

Covers multipart/form-data, parse_cookie, decode_signed_value, and the
escape helpers that applications commonly call on user input
(xhtml_escape, xhtml_unescape, linkify, url_escape). Each uses the worst
input found in a survey; all are well under their limits (multipart about
5 bytes per input byte, cookies and escapes about 20, signed values 4).

_parse_request_range and split_host_and_port make at most a few copies of
their input and keep no per-item structures, so they get no budget.

Merge pull request #3820 from bdarnell/claude/malformed-input-fixes

Return errors instead of crashing on two kinds of malformed input

Return errors instead of crashing on two kinds of malformed input

A Host header whose port has more digits than int() accepts (4300 by
default) raised ValueError from HTTPServerRequest, which was logged as an
uncaught exception and closed the connection without a response. It is
now a 400 like other invalid Host headers.

A permessage-deflate offer with an unsupported parameter, or a
max_window_bits that isn't an integer zlib accepts, failed the websocket
handshake with a 500 (plus a second exception during cleanup). The server
now declines that offer and considers the next one, as RFC 7692 section 5
requires. Compression is only enabled once both the compressor and
decompressor are created.

The compressor now rejects a window of 8 bits on every zlib version.
zlib 1.2.9 and later already did; older ones (as in manylinux2014)
silently used a 9-bit window instead, which a peer that asked for 8 bits
may be unable to decompress.
